strings.name: Michael Stonebraker
strings.role: Computer scientist · Database researcher and entrepreneur
strings.summary: Educated at Princeton and Michigan, Stonebraker spent decades researching databases at Berkeley before moving to MIT. With teams he developed Ingres, Postgres and architectures for different workloads, translating research into several companies. His work connects system design, open software and commercial applications; more recently he has worked on DBOS and reliable workflows.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: His work advanced relational and newer database systems, connecting research, open-source software and industrial applications.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Electrical engineering degree, Princeton (1965); doctorate, University of Michigan (1971).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Ingres and Postgres
strings.highlights.h1.text: With teams, he put relational data management and extensible object-relational systems into practice.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Designing for workloads
strings.highlights.h2.text: Projects including C-Store used different architectures for analytics, transactions and scientific data.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Reliable workflows
strings.timeline.t1.text: A DBOS article argued for organizing middleware around workflows, including failure recovery for AI applications.
strings.timeline.t2.title: DBOS publicly launches
strings.timeline.t2.text: The company he co-founded announced seed funding to apply database research to reliable cloud applications.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Turing Award announced
strings.timeline.t3.text: Named the 2014 recipient for contributions to modern database systems.
strings.timeline.t4.title: C-Store paper
strings.timeline.t4.text: A multi-university team proposed a column-oriented database optimized for reading and analytics.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Postgres design published
strings.timeline.t5.text: With Lawrence Rowe, he described a successor system supporting complex objects and extensibility.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Ingres system paper
strings.timeline.t6.text: With Eugene Wong and colleagues, he explained relational database design, implementation and trade-offs.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Doctoral training completed
strings.timeline.t7.text: He earned his Michigan doctorate and joined Berkeley's academic community in this period.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Princeton degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: He earned an electrical engineering degree before continuing graduate study.
